research_question: What is the evidence-based, teachable theory of COGNITIVE LOAD and SIMPLICITY in UI/web design — Hick's Law, Miller's Law, cognitive-load theory, choice overload, recognition-over-recall, progressive disclosure, KISS, Tesler's Law — and what mechanically-checkable PASS/FAIL rules can an AI design-review agent apply to reduce mental effort on a rendered Next/Tailwind/Radix/shadcn page?
openai_instructions: Focus on logical deduction: formalize each law (Hick's RT = a + b*log2(n); Miller's 7±2 / chunking; intrinsic vs extraneous vs germane load), derive the design implication of each, and translate to a checkable assertion (e.g. primary screen surfaces <= N primary actions; forms chunk fields into labeled groups; recognition affordances over free-recall entry). Build the failure tree of an overloaded interface. Cite NN/g #6 + #8 heuristics and Laws of UX primary pages.
claude_instructions: Investigate the contrarian angle: when does removing options or hiding behind progressive disclosure HURT (power users, Tesler's law of conservation of complexity, hidden critical actions, oversimplification that adds steps)? Cross-verify Hick's-law claims (it applies to known equiprobable choices, not all menus). Find measurable proxies an agent can compute (count of simultaneous primary CTAs, count of form fields, nav item count, density).
search_strategy: hicks law number of choices decision time
millers law chunking 7 plus minus 2 ux
choice overload paradox of choice ui

required_output_schema.per_finding_format: claim, evidence, confidence (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW), source URLs, counter-evidence

phases.name: Landscape
phases.objective: Survey the canonical cognitive-load & simplicity laws
sub_questions: What are the established laws (Hick, Miller, cognitive-load theory, choice overload, Tesler) and what does each precisely claim?
How do NN/g's recognition-over-recall and aesthetic-minimalist heuristics frame simplicity?
phases.evidence_priorities: Laws of UX primary pages, NN/g heuristics #6 and #8, cognitive-load theory sources
phases.stop_condition: Complete when all major laws are defined with sources and precise statements

phases.name: Mechanics
phases.objective: How to reduce load in a real interface
sub_questions: What techniques operationalize each law (chunking, progressive disclosure, smart defaults, recognition affordances, subtract-before-add) in a Tailwind/shadcn build?
What computed proxies make load measurable (primary-action count, field count, nav breadth, choices-per-decision)?
phases.evidence_priorities: NN/g progressive disclosure, form simplification studies, default-selection research
phases.stop_condition: Complete when concrete techniques + 2+ measurable proxies documented

phases.name: Failure Modes
phases.objective: What overload looks like and how it reads
sub_questions: What are the named failure modes (choice overload, wall of options, mandatory recall, dense screens, redundant steps) and the user symptom of each?
How can a reviewer detect each from the rendered page?
phases.evidence_priorities: abandonment, decision paralysis, error rate, time-on-task
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 5+ failure modes with detection signals documented

phases.name: Contrarian
sub_questions: When does subtraction/hiding hurt (Tesler's law, hidden critical actions, power-user efficiency, oversimplification adding steps)?
phases.evidence_priorities: conservation of complexity, hidden-action discoverability, expert vs novice tradeoff
phases.stop_condition: Complete when 2+ substantive counter-arguments with evidence found
